title: Reject self-contradicting readings; make the changelog entry a default
summary: Add a code check, run when a reading is parsed (and again at admission), that a file-scope criterion ("only these files change") agrees with the deliverables list. Add a `changelog` default to defaults.toml and the reader prompt so CHANGELOG.md is listed as a deliverable and never excluded for code, docs, config and build changes.

defaults_applied.how: The fix is a code check at the point readings are built, plus a default, rather than another prompt reminder.
Consistency is enforced in code at parse and admission, not left to the verifier.
Unit tests cover the consistent and contradictory cases; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One focused change: one consistency check, one default.
The check's error messages and the default text are plain and self-explanatory.

assumptions: The check is a heuristic over criterion text: a criterion that says only/exclusively/no other files change, and names paths, must name every deliverable path, and must not name a file that is outside the deliverables list as allowed. It is not a full natural-language parse.
CHANGELOG.md is a deliverable for every reading whose class is code, tests, docs, config, build or prompts. Design and other readings are exempt, as are readings with no capability.

A contradiction in build_reading is returned as an error with a message naming the file, so the reader is re-prompted or fails before the user sees the reading. Admission re-checks the accepted reading as a backstop.

Adding a default changes defaults.toml, which is governance. It is therefore a listed deliverable and is named in a criterion. The defaults version is bumped if the repository's convention requires it for added entries.

acceptance_criteria.text: A function in crates/athena-core (reading consistency check) returns an error naming the file when a criterion that restricts the change to named files omits a deliverable path, or when a deliverables list contains CHANGELOG.md while a criterion excludes it.

build_reading in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs calls the check after the deliverables are normalized, so a contradictory reading is rejected before it is recorded or shown; admission.rs also calls it on the accepted reading.

defaults.toml gains a `changelog` default, applying to code, tests, docs, config, build and prompts, which says every change adds a CHANGELOG.md entry; defaults.toml is named in this criterion as an intended change.
crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md tells the reader to list CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable and to keep file-scope criteria consistent with the deliverables list.
CHANGELOG.md gains an entry for this change.

Run `cargo test` and confirm the new unit tests pass: consistent scope accepted, scope omitting a deliverable rejected, scope excluding CHANGELOG.md while it is listed rejected, and a reading with no scope criterion accepted.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.

out_of_scope: Changing the verifier's behavior or prompts.
Rewriting past jobs' records or the four failed jobs.
Parsing arbitrary natural-language criteria beyond the file-scope pattern.
departures: The change touches parsing, admission, defaults and the prompt, and the heuristic needs several tests. I therefore set cost and time above the reference and the pass probability slightly lower. I read only part of the code; defaults.rs, records.rs and briefs.rs are uncertain deliverables.
